record_title: Explicit PFR translate covers are oracle-hard even below doubling two
provenance: An oracle-complexity consequence of the explicit-output convention in recent algorithmic Polynomial Freiman--Ruzsa theorems, proved using a hidden-outlier small-doubling family and a quotient-dimension bound for coset covers.
limitations: The lower bound concerns explicit lists of translate representatives under uniform-sample plus point-membership access. It does not apply to subspace-only output, stronger access oracles, or compressed symbolic cover descriptions. The proof is short, so folklore and near-simultaneous priority risk remain material.
